data.title: Mondelez takes a majority stake in Undercover Snacks
data.description:
Mondelez International (MDLZ) became a majority investor in better-for-you snack company Undercover Snacks. 

Undercover Snacks is known for creating delicious treats with healthy ingredients in disguise, including its signature chocolate and frosted quinoa crisps. All Undercover products are non-GMO, certified gluten-free, and produced at the company's dedicated peanut-free, tree-nut-free facility in East Hanover, New Jersey. 

The company began as an entrepreneurial startup and has grown into a nationally recognized brand sold in more than 25K retail locations and enjoyed by millions of travelers each month on United Airlines (UAL). The current distribution network includes grocery, mass, club, drug, foodservice, and e-commerce channels. Its products are sold at leading retailers, including Whole Foods Market, Target, Walmart, Kroger, CVS, Walgreens, Sprouts, and Albertsons, as well as Amazon (AMZN). The company will continue to operate as a standalone business led by its existing management team while gaining access to Mondelez's (MDLZ) extensive capabilities, resources, and expertise to accelerate innovation, distribution, and long-term growth.

data.title: Nasdaq suffers a 3% loss as investors rotate out of technology
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) declined 3% on Friday due to a continued technology rout intensified by Intel’s (INTC) disappointing third-quarter earnings results and other semiconductor positions being sold.

The tech-heavy index is on track for its worst single-day performance since June.

Shares of semiconductor giant Intel (INTC) dropped more than 30% after its third-quarter results showed guidance that missed Wall Street estimates by a considerable margin.

Other semiconductors, including Sandisk (SNDK), CoreWeave (CRWV), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and QUALCOMM (QCOM) also declined more than 10%.

Here are the stocks leading the decline in the Nasdaq:

data.title: Gates anticipates $1.66-$1.72 2026 adjusted EPS while aiming for 6.5% Q4 core growth
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Gates Industrial Corporation Ltd. (GTES) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "In the third quarter, we generated mid-single-digit core sales growth, consistent with our guidance, and delivered strong adjusted EBITDA margin, which approached 24%." (CEO & Director Ivo Jurek)
  • "Given our performance year-to-date and current demand trends, we are raising our full year adjusted earnings per share guidance." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Third quarter sales were approximately $904 million" and "Adjusted EBITDA margin increased 90 basis points to a company record of 23.8%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "In Power Transmission, sales were approximately $560 million" with "adjusted EBITDA margin of 24.5%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "In Fluid Power, sales were approximately $343 million" and "Our data center revenues increased about 2.5x compared to the last year's third quarter." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Adjusted EPS increased from $0.39 per share in the prior year quarter to a record $0.47 per share." (Executive VP & CFO L. Mallard)

Outlook

  • "We have narrowed our full year core sales growth to a range of 3.2% to 3.8%" and "We now anticipate full year adjusted EBITDA to be in the range of $809 million to $823 million." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • "We have updated our full year adjusted earnings per share to a range of $1.66 per share to $1.72 per share" and "For the fourth quarter, we estimate total sales to be in the range of $905 million to $925 million and core revenue growth to be approximately 6.5% at the midpoint." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • "We are reiterating our expectation for second half core sales growth to approximately 6% at the midpoint as well as second half adjusted EBITDA margin to measure approximately 23.5%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • Compared with Q2, management shifted from raising full-year core-sales-growth guidance to "maintaining the 3.5% midpoint" while increasing adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS ranges. (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)

Financial Results

  • "Third quarter sales were approximately $904 million" with "core growth of 5.5%." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Adjusted EBITDA was $215 million" and "Adjusted earnings per share increased approximately 21% to a quarterly record of $0.47." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • "Our trailing 12-month free cash flow conversion was 82%" and "Our net leverage ratio ended the quarter at 1.8x." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • "We repurchased approximately $57 million worth of our shares in the third quarter" and "Our return on invested capital was 21.5% on a trailing 12-month basis." (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)

Q&A

  • Stephen Volkmann, Jefferies: asked why Q4 margin steps down with faster growth; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "we do see some normal seasonality," plus "a little bit of dilution from a price/cost perspective" and "a significant increase in our variable comp... mostly hits in Q4."
  • Stephen Volkmann, Jefferies: asked about M&A valuations; CEO & Director Jurek: "we're going to be very disciplined" and "we will do deals" that "generate appropriate returns" and "be accretive."
  • Jeffrey Hammond, KeyBanc: asked about price/cost differences between segments; CEO & Director Jurek: "we are making bigger investments" and said FP is performing "absent" investment effects.
  • Nigel Coe, Wolfe: asked early view on 2027; CEO & Director Jurek: "the setup is really developing quite nicely" and said the company will outline 2027 thinking on "November 19."
  • Nigel Coe, Wolfe: asked data center product pipeline and inventory pickup; CEO & Director Jurek: "pretty significant increase in the product launches" across "hoses... pumps... coupling"; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: inventory includes "safety stock" and said pricing collection supports confidence in "90-plus percent conversion number."
  • Jeffrey Hammond, KeyBanc: asked North America drags and auto trends; CEO & Director Jurek: "auto OE was down slightly" and "AR was up slightly" while industrial OEM growth was "in the 20s" and industrial aftermarket accelerated "into the low teens."
  • Andrew Kaplowitz, Citi: asked about enterprise initiatives 2.0; CEO & Director Jurek: "we will certainly provide you a window" but "much more focusing on delivering above-market growth rate"; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "we are super focused on growth as we move forward."
  • Andrew Kaplowitz, Citi: asked personal mobility visibility; CEO & Director Jurek: "We have a terrific visibility" and said trajectory is "driving that 20% to 30% growth rate."
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan: asked data center right-to-win and engagement; CEO & Director Jurek: referenced "production ramp-up of our e-water pumps" and working with "a couple of hyperscalers" and "infrastructure builders."
  • Tomohiko Sano, JPMorgan: asked NPI/R&D allocation; CEO & Director Jurek: "we've made some anticipated expectations that we're going to get into the low 20s in NPI vitality."
  • David Raso, Evercore: asked off-highway/customer inventory and pricing; CEO & Director Jurek: off-highway was "somewhat mixed" with construction strength and ag "flattish to maybe just slightly down"; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "our 80/20 tools" are improving "analytical pricing."
  • David Raso, Evercore: asked variable comp drag uniqueness; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "this year is a little bit more normalized" and last year "lower than normal"; CEO & Director Jurek: "we are printing record results."
  • Jerry Revich, Wells Fargo: asked implied Q4 margin headwinds; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: watch "more dilutive... price/cost" as "higher-cost inventory continues to move through."
  • Jerry Revich, Wells Fargo: asked margin upside beyond 2027 targets; CEO & Director Jurek: margin upside comes from "enterprise initiatives" plus "a nice component of volume."
  • Christopher Dankert, D.A. Davidson: asked about the belts acquisition; CEO & Director Jurek: closed "beginning of Q4" with "diminutive" Q4 revenue, "more meaningful" in 2027 at "about 100 bps, plus or minus" of revenue, and profitability "dilutive" initially with a plan to reach "company average profitability" in "the next 12 months."
  • Brandon Knutson, Morgan Stanley: asked personal mobility acceleration and capacity for mobility/data center; CEO & Director Jurek: mobility growth was "broad-based" and capacity is "in place"; for data center, "We are investing in R&D... production scale-up... adding capacity."
  • Brandon Knutson, Morgan Stanley: asked to quantify growth investments; Executive VP & CFO Mallard: "we don't really quantify the different pieces and the parts."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts were slightly skeptical on near-term margins, cash/inventory, and the Q4 guide framing, including "margin stepping down" (Stephen Volkmann, Jefferies) and "beatable implied 4Q guide" (Jerry Revich, Wells Fargo).
  • Management tone was slightly positive and forward-leaning on growth, repeatedly pointing to durability and optionality, including "the setup is really developing quite nicely" (CEO & Director Jurek) and "significant optionality to deploy capital" (Executive VP & CFO Mallard).
  • Versus Q2, management confidence language shifted from "early stages of an industrial recovery" to acceleration, including "Relative to the second quarter, our industrial core growth accelerated" (CEO & Director Jurek) and a clearer tilt toward "strategic inorganic investments." (CEO & Director Jurek)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q3 emphasized acceleration and North America inflection, including "North America inflected positively" and "industrial core growth accelerated to high single digits from mid-single digits." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • Q2 focused on entering recovery and raising broad guidance, including "we believe that we have entered the early stages of an industrial recovery" and "we have raised our 2026 full year guidance for core sales growth and profitability." (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • Q3 guidance changes were more targeted: "maintaining the 3.5% midpoint" core-sales-growth outlook while increasing adjusted EBITDA and adjusted EPS ranges, compared with Q2 raising core-sales-growth, EBITDA, and EPS guidance together. (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • Analyst focus shifted from ERP and pricing mechanics in Q2 to Q4 margin cadence, inventories, M&A, and integration of the belts acquisition in Q3.

Risks and Concerns

  • "Some normal seasonality" and "less working days" were cited as Q4 margin headwinds, alongside "a little bit of dilution from a price/cost perspective" and a Q4 "variable comp" step-up. (Executive VP & CFO Mallard)
  • Management pointed to end-market mix risk, noting North America "auto OE was down slightly" and agriculture remained weak, described as "flattish to maybe just slightly down" in Q3. (CEO & Director Jurek)
  • On the belts acquisition, management flagged near-term profitability dilution, saying profitability "was dilutive" and requires execution to reach "company average profitability" within "the next 12 months." (CEO & Director Jurek)

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q3 as a quarter of accelerating industrial demand, record profitability metrics, and a stronger North America trend, while raising full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $1.66-$1.72 and holding the full-year core-sales-growth midpoint at 3.5%. Executives highlighted ongoing investments in data centers and personal mobility, a more active interest in disciplined M&A, and a newly closed belts acquisition expected to contribute more meaningfully in 2027, with margin seasonality, price/cost normalization, and variable compensation identified as key drivers shaping Q4 profitability cadence.

data.title: Rio Tinto begins restart of Oyu Tolgoi underground operations after seismic event
data.description:
Rio Tinto (RIO) said Friday it is progressively restarting underground operations at the Oyu Tolgoi copper mine in Mongolia after completing safety reviews following a seismic event that ​temporarily halted mining activities.

Rio (RIO) said ​a seismic event triggered ⁠a localized rockfall in a temporary storage ​area adjacent to the production zone, causing ​ground vibrations but resulting in no structural damage to the underground cave or operating infrastructure; two employees continue to receive treatment for non-life-threatening injuries.

The company has been ramping up underground mining at Oyu Tolgoi, where open-pit operations began in 2011, but the most valuable copper resources lie underground.

A pause on underground operations at Oyu Tolgoi is unlikely to have a long-term impact on the project's production, but "a core question that this event generates is, 'What is the long-term sustainable rate of cave propagation, and does it align with the targeted production rate?" Jefferies analysts said in a note.

The Oyu Tolgoi underground uses block caving, a process that stresses the surrounding rock, and Jefferies wonders whether such events could change the way investors value different mining techniques.

"For those generalists not frightened from the sector by mining disruptions, we do think that we will start to see further premiums paid for lower-risk mining methods," the bank wrote.

Rio (RIO) owns a 66% stake in Oyu Tolgoi, one ​of the world's largest known copper ​and gold deposits, with the Mongolian government holding the rest.

data.title: Cracks in the cart: Consumer staples hit a wall as inflation outpaces sales
data.description:
The narrative of the “resilient consumer” is breaking down as major consumer staples (XLP) companies increasingly deliver organic revenue growth that lags the pace of inflation, according to Sakonnet Research.

While packaged goods giants posted organic sales growth between 7% and 9% across North America in 2022 and early 2023, the pace slowed considerably once pricing actions peaked and volumes softened, analyst Adam Josephson noted.

By 2024 and 2025, average organic growth across the sector flattened to near zero.

Through the first three quarters of 2026, that weakness has solidified. Average organic sales across 20 staples manufacturers grew by just 2% in the first quarter and decelerated to 1% in both the second and third quarters.

While several beverage and personal care brands such as Coca-Cola (KO), Procter & Gamble (PG), and Church & Dwight (CHD) maintained modest gains, packaged food manufacturers—including General Mills (GIS), Kraft Heinz (KHC), Conagra (CAG), and Campbell's (CPB)—recorded recurring contractions in their North American business.

On the inflation front, the Consumer Price Index advanced 3.7% Y/Y in September as energy costs surged. The core CPI measure, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, grew 2.6% from a year ago and remains above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

data.title: U.S. Department of Justice said to be aware of Binance hack reports
data.description:
U.S. Department of Justice is aware of the reports surrounding the Binance hack, and the Secret Service is investigating the matter with private-sector partners, including Circle (CRCL), Bloomberg News reported, citing an emailed statement.

Secret Service is looking to identify, freeze, trace, and recover funds stolen from Binance, according to the statement.

Separately, a person familiar with the situation told Reuters that Binance is ‌working with law enforcement around the world, including the Federal ​Bureau of Investigation.

The theft of $6.3B of assets from Binance, constituting the world's largest crypto hack, was conducted by a North Korean cybercrime group, according to two crypto analysis firms' assessment.

The world's largest crypto exchange had frozen about $3B of its $6.3B in assets affected by a massive hack, and was expecting to freeze more. At about noon, Binance said withdrawals are expected to resume within the next 42 hours.

The attack, which took place on Thursday, started with a compromised laptop belonging to an employee. Binance's investigation identified additional points of breach, indicating the incident went beyond one device.

The exchange didn't find any evidence that wallet private keys were compromised. The company assured that its users won't bear any losses. "All losses will be covered in full by its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds," it said.

Crypto stocks were trading lower after the news: Coinbase Global (COIN) -13.34% to $139.16; Hut 8 (HUT) -13.18% to $57.68; Bullish (BLSH) -12.05% to $25.04; Cipher Digital (CIFR) -12.04% to $7.13; IREN (IREN) -10.32% to $23.54; Bakkt (BKKT) -10.24% to $4.56; and Riot Platforms (RIOT) -10.08% to $12.36.

data.title: Anthropic may get junk credit rating after its IPO, Blackstone says: report
data.description:
• Anthropic (ANT) may receive a high-yield, or junk, credit rating after its IPO, which can complicate the AI company's plans to borrow money to fund its growing infrastructure spending, according to a media report. 
  • Blackstone (BX), an anchor investor in Anthropic's $63B chip financing deal known as Project North Star, has told investors that the company is more likely to receive a rating in the double-B range or higher, according to the Financial Times report.
  • An investment-grade rating would allow Anthropic to borrow at lower costs to finance its artificial intelligence infrastructure projects.
  • Anthropic has more than $112B in cash and equivalents, while investors expect the company could raise about $100B through its IPO, the report said.

data.title: ‘Don’t rule out further drawdowns’ in tech as current cycle hits 22 drawdowns in only two years – Turning Point Market Research
data.description:
The technology sectors have already seen 22 drawdowns in performance since 2024, while the 1995-2000 tech bubble had 36 in total, according to Turning Point Market Research analysts.

Currently, the average public tech stock is down 37.1% from its 52-week high, due to the ongoing sell-off across AI stocks (AIQ), semiconductors (SMH), (XSD), and the overall technology sector (XLK), (VGT).

From 1995 to 2000, technology sub-industries experienced 36 independent drawdowns of 20% or more, compared with 22 since 2024, Turning Point Market Research analysts noted.

Within the technology sub-industries, internet services and infrastructure saw 10 drawdowns between 1995 and 2000, and only one from 2024 until now.

The biggest drawdowns in the past two years were in electronic components and semiconductors. Each sub-sector saw three.

The deepest drawdown in recent years in semiconductors (SMH), (XSD) was -35.1%.

 

 

 

“With that in mind, don't rule out further, potentially more painful drawdowns,” Turning Point analysts said. “Drawdowns are a common feature of major innovation cycles.”

data.title: Bispecific biotech Bambusa and Parkinson’s-focused Aspen slide on trading debuts
data.description:
Bambusa Therapeutics (BBTX), developer of bispecific antibody therapies, and Aspen Neuroscience (ASPE), a cell therapy developer focused on Parkinson’s disease, traded lower on Friday as their shares made listing debuts on Nasdaq.

Boston-based Bambusa started trading at $14.88 at about 11.00 am ET, implying roughly a 7% decline from its IPO price of $16.00 per share, which raised the company approximately $168.9M.  

On Thursday, the company upsized the offering to ~10.6M shares compared with its initial plans to sell 9.4M shares at $15-$17, which would have generated $150.4M in gross proceeds at the midpoint.

Bambusa (BBTX) expects to use net proceeds together with its existing cash resources primarily to advance its lead asset, BBT001, which is set to enter mid-stage development for Alzheimer's disease this year.

San Diego-based Aspen (ASPE), whose backers include Gilead Sciences (GILD), opened for trading at $14.70 at about 11:40 am ET before reaching $12.00 about an hour later to indicate roughly a 20% drop from the IPO price of $15.00.

On Thursday, the company priced the offering of ~9.4M shares at the low end of its marketed range, aiming to raise about $140.6M in gross proceeds, which it intends to use mainly to advance its lead product candidate, sasineprocel.

The one-time therapy is currently undergoing a Phase 1/2a trial for mid-stage to moderately advanced Parkinson’s disease, ahead of a late-stage trial initiation in H2 2027, subject to regulatory feedback.

data.title: FedEx Freight rallies on Q3 results and improved outlook for transition period
data.description:
Shares of FedEx Freight (FDXF) were launched higher Friday after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter results and raising its outlook for the transition period ending on December 31.

“While we are in the early stages of our journey as an independent company, we are encouraged by the momentum we are seeing across our operational, commercial, and technology initiatives. Guided by a clear and consistent strategy, we remain confident in the opportunities ahead and our ability to continue strengthening the business for long-term success,” FedEx Freight CEO John Smith said on Thursday.

For the four-month period ending September 30, revenue grew 9.2% as revenue per shipment increased 10.1% primarily by higher fuel surcharges, greater weight per shipment, and an increase in base revenue per hundredweight. Excluding fuel surcharges, revenue per shipment was up a much more modest 1.6%.

Higher costs to operate the standalone business, compensation and merit-related expenses, and expenses tied to separating FedEx Freight (FDXF) from FedEx (FDX) drove operating income down 6.1% to $383M. However, stripping out certain charges, adjusted operating income was up 16.4% to $510M, translating into a 90-basis-point expansion in the company’s operating margin to 15.5%. 

At the same time, unadjusted earnings declined by 43%, but increased 24.6% to $2.15 on an adjusted basis.

For the current 3-month quarter, FedEx Freight (FDXF) expects to earn an adjusted profit of $0.65 and $0.75 per share on $2.30B and $2.37B in sales. This compares to estimates of $0.54 and $2.23B, respectively.

For the 7-month transition period ending on December 31, revenue is expected to be between $5.58B and $5.65B, up from original guidance for an increase of 4% to 6%. This includes $2.3B and $2.37B in sales for the final three months of 2026 versus estimates of $2.23B.

Earnings for the transition period ending December 31 are expected to be between $2.80 and $2.90 per share, up from a prior forecast of $2.40 and $2.60 per share.
